what: H7 two-plane census out of sample (F23): how many honest co-registration cohorts the RELATION plane alone flags, how many reach the IMPACT floor (>=4 distinct shards of one repo), and how many the full two-plane rule (adds partition P<1.6) pages. Shows H4's two-plane principle a second time (v1's 0 vs 2,926 honest pages was the first).
re_derived: read-only with h7_score.py's load + cohorts + partition logic (prototypes/h7_score.py); thresholds k=5, W=600 s, IMPACT=4, PMAX=1.6. Backs facts-55.md F23.

combined_301_305.note: 0 of 7 past-floor honest cohorts paged out of sample. Every honest cohort that reached the impact floor had partition P >= 1.86, well above the 1.6 line -- the partition plane, not co-registration, did the separating.

two_plane_principle: Co-registration ALONE (the relation plane) would flag 12 honest cohorts over 301-305 (7 + 5); 7 of them reach the impact floor. Adding the partition plane (P<1.6) pages 0 of those 7 -- honest cohorts overlap on popular shards (P 1.86-3.25), while the swarm partitions (P~1.0). This is the same 'requiring two planes makes victim-side detection affordable' result as v1's 0 vs 2,926 (H4), measured a second way.
caveats: Offline (whole-run pooling), small n. The P=1.86 cohort on 301-302 is the closest honest approach to the 1.6 line in this census; the out-of-sample margin risk (calibration min 1.64; one P=1.59 cohort on 303 cleared by the FRESH gate) is reported in results/evade_rate_gemini31.json. Thresholds were set on the 8 calibration weeks (in-sample), reported separately.
